name: 3-Card Brag
description: 3-Card Brag is Britain's premier vying (betting) card game and a direct ancestor of modern Poker. Each player receives three cards and competes for a central pot. Its most distinctive feature is the 'Blind' betting system, where a player can bet without looking at their cards for half the cost, maintaining a psychological and mechanical advantage over 'Seeing' players. It is fast, aggressive, and deeply rooted in British pub and gambling traditions.

history.origins: Brag emerged in 16th-century England as a three-card vying game. It evolved into the parent of Indian Teen Patti and influenced the betting structures of early American Poker variants like Three-Card Poker.
timeline: 1500s: Early versions of 'Post and Pair' and Brag documented in England.
1700s: The 'Bragger' (wild card) mechanic is introduced, usually the Jack of Clubs.
1900s: Remains the standard gambling game in British military and social clubs.
Present: A cultural staple of British pub life and high-stakes private games.
history.cultural: Symbolizes 'working class' poker in the UK; featured in numerous British films like 'Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels'.
history.evolution: The game's hand rankings (Prial > Running Flush > Run) and the half-price blind betting have remained largely consistent for centuries, despite the global dominance of Poker.

setup.dealing: Every player contributes an ante. Dealer deals three cards face-down to each player.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, betting chips or currency.

rules.objective: Win the pot by holding the best three-card combination or by being the last player remaining after others fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Blind/See**: Players decide whether to bet 'Blind' (unseen) or 'See' their cards. 2. **Betting**: Blind players bet N; Seeing players must bet at least 2N. 3. **Folding**: A player can fold at any time, losing all previous contributions. 4. **Showdown**: If only two players remain, one can 'See' the other by paying double the current bet to compare hands. 5. **Hand Ranks**: Prial (Three of a Kind), Running Flush (Straight Flush), Run (Straight), Flush, Pair, High Card.
keyRules: Prial of 3s is the highest possible hand (3-3-3 beats A-A-A).
A Blind player's hand beats a Seeing player's identical hand (Blind advantage).
A Seeing player can only 'See' a player when only two people remain in the hand.

strategy.basic: Stay Blind as long as possible. Betting half-price allows you to build the pot while making it expensive for Seeing players to stay in with marginal hands.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Prial' Hunt: If you hold a pair of 3s, you are statistically likely to have the best hand. If you hold a 3 and a wild card ('Bragger'), your hand is incredibly strong.
strategy.advanced: Range Inference: Watch the Betting Speed. A player who sees their cards and immediately raises is often representing a Run or better. A player who stays Blind for many rounds is either bluffing or has complete confidence in the shuffle.
tips: Never 'See' your cards too early; the psychological pressure of a Blind player is your best weapon.
If you are a Seeing player, don't chase a Blind bet unless you have at least a Flush.

variations.name: Brag with Braggers
variations.description: Standard variant where J♣, 9♦, and A♦ are wild cards (Braggers).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant notes wild-card options, but engine-level overrides for card behavior are not yet modeled.

scoring.winCondition: Last player standing OR best hand at showdown.

synthesis.shortDescription: Britain's oldest gambling card game and the ancestor of Teen Patti and Poker. Three cards. Braggers (wilds). A blind bet that costs half price. Pure nerve versus pure hand strength.
